interface.signature: def articulationPoints(V: int, adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:

preconditions.description: V is an integer representing the number of vertices, within the range [1, 10^5].
adj is a list of length V, where each element is the adjacency list for a vertex.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(neighbors, list) and all(isinstance(n, int) and 0 <= n < V for n in neighbors) for neighbors in adj)
preconditions.description: Each adjacency list contains only integers representing valid vertex indices from 0 to V-1.
The graph represented by V and adj is undirected and connected. Loops (edges from a vertex to itself) may exist.

postconditions.expression: isinstance(return_value, list) and all(isinstance(x, int) for x in return_value)
postconditions.description: The return value is a list of integers.
The returned list of vertices is sorted in ascending order.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == 0 or (return_value == [-1] and all(not is_articulation(V, adj, v) for v in range(V)))
postconditions.description: If no articulation points exist, the list contains exactly [-1]. Otherwise, it contains exactly the set of articulation points.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) > 0 and return_value[0] != -1 implies all(is_articulation(V, adj, v) for v in return_value) and all(not is_articulation(V, adj, v) for v in range(V) if v not in return_value)
postconditions.description: If the list does not contain -1, it contains exactly all vertices v such that removing v (and its incident edges) increases the number of connected components in the graph.
